concepts.label: OrphanReporter (aggregated logging of orphaned/timed-out requests)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a third distinct SDK observability mechanism alongside sdk:logging-meter and sdk:request-tracer: it only fires for responses whose original caller has already stopped listening, and works purely through built-in logging with no external-system plug-in point

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a component observed through a named metric/endpoint/log surface
relations.evidence: The way it works is that every time a response is in the process of being completed, when the SDK detects that the original caller is not listening anymore (likely because of a timeout), it will send this "orphaned" response to a reporting utility which aggregates all responses and in regular intervals logs them in a specific format.

relations.subject: sdk:orphan-reporter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate whose object is frequently a literal rather than a concept
relations.evidence: By default they will be aggregated and logged every 10 seconds, but the event will be skipped if there are no orphans to report.

relations.subject: sdk:orphan-reporter
relations.object: an emitted log entry when there are no orphans to report in the current interval
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a monitoring/logging mechanism deliberately omitting something from what it records
relations.evidence: By default they will be aggregated and logged every 10 seconds, but the event will be skipped if there are no orphans to report.

relations.subject: sdk:orphan-reporter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a behavior that is off by default and needs an explicit config flag
relations.evidence: If you want to enable the new output format, for now you have to set the `com.couchbase.orphanReporterNewOutputFormat` system property to `true`.

notable_absence.finding: The page states you can 'look for the output of the OrphanReporter and correlate' a TimeoutException with it, and that each entry carries a Channel ID field explicitly 'to correlate with the server logs', but never links to where those server-side logs or their own connection/channel identifiers are documented - the correlation is described as possible from the client side only, with the other end of it left completely unlinked.

cross_component_finding: The orphan-log entry's Channel ID field ('c': 'The Channel ID to correlate with the server logs') is explicitly designed to let an operator join a client-side orphaned-request log line to the corresponding entry in Couchbase Server's own logs - the only field in either JSON output format whose stated purpose is cross-component correlation rather than describing the request itself.
